# Whole-house battery backup without solar

**Yes, you can install a whole-house battery backup system without solar panels.** It's often called a *standalone home battery*, *grid-charged battery*, or *solar-free home energy storage system*.

The battery charges from the electrical grid when power is available and automatically supplies electricity to your home during an outage.

<AsyncImageGroup query={["Tesla Powerwall 3 mounted garage home battery installation","FranklinWH aPower home battery installed wall","Enphase IQ Battery home wall mounted installation"]} aspectRatio="5:4" layout="carousel" shop_eligible={true}/>

## How it works

<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={2}>
  <svg viewBox="0 0 340 174" width="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
    {#each [{x:8,label:"Utility grid",sub:"Charges battery"},{x:123,label:"Home battery",sub:"Stores energy"},{x:238,label:"Your home",sub:"Backup power"}] as n,i}
      <rect x={n.x} y="27" width="94" height="94" rx="10" fill={i===1?"#DDECE6":"#EDF0F3"} stroke={i===1?"#43866D":"#BCC5CE"}/>
      {#if i===0}
        <path d="M40 95 L55 50 L70 95 M46 80 H64 M43 67 H67" stroke="#526477" strokeWidth="3" fill="none"/>
      {:else if i===1}
        <rect x="152" y="48" width="37" height="55" rx="4" fill="none" stroke="#287957" strokeWidth="3"/>
        <path d="M173 57 L163 77 H173 L166 94" stroke="#287957" strokeWidth="3" fill="none"/>
      {:else}
        <path d="M255 76 L285 51 L315 76 V104 H255 Z M276 104 V84 H294 V104" fill="none" stroke="#526477" strokeWidth="3"/>
      {/if}
      <text x={n.x+47} y="137" fontSize="11" fontWeight="600" textAnchor="middle" fill="currentColor">{n.label}</text>
      <text x={n.x+47} y="151" fontSize="9" textAnchor="middle" fill="currentColor">{n.sub}</text>
    {/each}
    <path d="M103 74 H119 M115 70 L120 74 L115 78 M218 74 H234 M230 70 L235 74 L230 78" stroke="#287957" strokeWidth="2.5" fill="none" strokeLinecap="round"/>
    <text x="170" y="12" textAnchor="middle" fontSize="10" fill="currentColor">No solar panels required</text>
  </svg>
  <text color="secondary" size="xs" textAlign="center">Conceptual diagram; actual installations also require appropriate switching, controls, and electrical protection.</text>
</box>

- **Normal operation:** The battery charges from the grid, potentially during cheaper off-peak hours.
- **Power outage:** The system disconnects safely from the grid and powers your home.
- **Grid restoration:** The system resumes normal operation and recharges.

You can also use the battery to reduce electricity costs if your utility has time-of-use pricing.

## Best battery systems to consider

| System | Capacity per unit | Continuous output | Best for |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| <Entity category="product" value="Tesla Powerwall 3"/> | 13.5 kWh | 11.5 kW | High-power home backup |
| <Entity category="product" value="FranklinWH aPower 2"/> | 15 kWh | 10 kW | Grid-only backup and expansion |
| <Entity category="product" value="Enphase IQ Battery 5P"/> | 5 kWh | 3.84 kW | Modular battery capacity |

FranklinWH explicitly supports operation without solar, including grid charging and automatic outage backup. <Cite refs={["turn319009search0","turn319009search15"]}/> Tesla is another strong option, but confirm grid-charging permissions and the exact solar-free configuration before ordering.

## How much battery do you need?

Use this calculator to estimate backup duration. It assumes 90% of the stated capacity is available during an outage.

{@body const [capacity,setCapacity] = DIL.useState(30)}
{@body const [load,setLoad] = DIL.useState(1.5)}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    **Battery capacity**
    <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{capacity} kWh</text>
  </row>
  <slider min={10} max={60} step={5} value={capacity} onChange={setCapacity}/>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    **Average household power usage**
    <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{load.toFixed(1)} kW</text>
  </row>
  <slider min={0.5} max={6} step={0.5} value={load} onChange={setLoad}/>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">ESTIMATED BACKUP DURATION</text>
  <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{(capacity*0.9/load).toFixed(1)} hours</title>
  <box background="surface-secondary" height="12px" radius="full" clip>
    <box background="rgba(48,143,106,0.85)" height="100%" width={`${Math.min(100,capacity*0.9/load/48*100)}%`} radius="full"/>
  </box>
  <row justify="between">
    <caption>0 hours</caption>
    <caption>48 hours</caption>
  </row>
  <caption>Illustrative estimate. Actual runtime depends on usable capacity, efficiency, reserve settings, and appliance usage.</caption>
</box>

## Typical installed costs

For initial budgeting in the US, before any incentives:

| Battery capacity | Estimated installed cost |
|---|---:|
| 13–15 kWh | $12,000–$20,000 |
| 27–30 kWh | $22,000–$35,000 |
| 40–45 kWh | $32,000–$50,000+ |

These are broad planning estimates, not local installation quotes. Electrical-panel modifications, backup gateways, permitting, and load management can affect the total.

**Important:** Without solar or a generator, the battery cannot recharge during a prolonged grid outage.

## What I would recommend

For whole-house backup without solar, I'd start by comparing **two Tesla Powerwall 3 units** against **two FranklinWH aPower 2 units**. Both are worth evaluating for approximately 27–30 kWh of storage. Whether either can support your entire house depends on peak loads, especially air conditioning, EV charging, and electric heating.

One question that will help narrow this down:

{@body const [duration,setDuration] = DIL.useState("24")}

    <radio value="48">48 hours or longer</radio>
